newsitem.title: USA: Governors urge immigrants get benefits.
newsitem.headline: Governors urge immigrants get benefits.

text.p: The nation's governors said on Tuesday they would work with Congress to find a way to help immigrants who risk losing welfare benefits as a result of legislation passed last year.

Papering over a split among state executives, the National Governors' Association adopted a compromise policy at its winter meeting, calling on Congress and the White House to aid legal immigrants -- without reopening the welfare law.

The vague language was approved by a NGA committee in place of an original proposal specifically stating that elderly and disabled immigrants who were in the United States before the law took effect should remain eligible for federal Food Stamps and disability aid.

Republican governors, under pressure from congressional Republican leaders, balked at the idea of reopening the welfare law less than six months after it was signed into law by President Bill Clinton. The Republican Governors' Association voted on Saturday to oppose any reopening of the law.
Clinton's 1998 budget, to be sent to Congress on Thursday, includes funding to restore aid to legal immigrants.

The resolution adopted urged Congress and the administration to "ensure that the immigration system and its requirements are fair to both citizens and non-citizens and meet the needs of aged and disabled immigrants who cannot naturalise."
